A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAR framework and retain corresponding methods, experiments and figures. All pages are readable. v1 ends with references; v2 adds Appendices A–D, which are available for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Matterport3D generation and outpainting experiments, quantitative ablations, and qualitative generalization and editing results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 3–8.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds timing measurements, sensitivity studies, additional baseline comparisons, Structured3D experiments and quantitative zero-shot evaluations in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The MAR/VAE framework, conditioning procedure, consistency loss and dual-space circular padding remain unchanged. Removing the 'three-layer' MLP description, explaining its blocks and correcting padding slice notation do not establish an actual architecture or procedure change.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained Matterport3D experiments and SUN360 outpainting examples, v2 adds training and evaluation on synthetic indoor Structured3D, zero-shot outpainting on held-out Structured3D, and zero-shot text-to-panorama evaluation using SUN360 prompts. These substantially broaden the represented data and generalization scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 adds DiffPano and UniPano to Matterport3D text-to-panorama comparisons (Table 7) and StitchDiffusion to SUN360 seam-consistency evaluation. PanoDiff, already shown qualitatively on SUN360 in v1, additionally becomes a quantitative Matterport3D outpainting comparator (Table 8). The original comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: The original experimental settings are retained. New protocols include a 9,000/1,000 Structured3D training/test split, separate 100-prompt and 100-image zero-shot evaluations, controlled inference timing on one A100 with batch size 8, and evaluations varying AR steps, denoising steps, padding ratios and guidance strength.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds runtime sensitivity to AR steps and padding, denoising-step and guidance-strength ablations, quantitative distribution-shift tests, and analysis of polar blur using Structured3D and perspective projections. Figure 15 adds small-object failure cases. The original scaling, consistency-loss and padding analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experiments. The noise variances introduced in Appendix A concern theoretical modeling, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their scores. New results include PAR/PanFusion latency of 10.03/28.91 seconds per image (Table 5), PAR-0.3B/PanoLlama Structured3D FID of 47.02/125.35 (Table 10), and PAR/Diffusion360 zero-shot outpainting FID of 127.01/140.91 (Table 11). Additional sensitivity and qualitative findings expand the evidence without establishing improvements to the original scores.

T1.justification: Appendix A introduces spherical Gaussian-field assumptions, area-averaged ERP pixel definitions, and derivations claiming independence with latitude-dependent variance (Equations 10–14). v1 contains no corresponding proof. This is a substantial theoretical addition, although the covariance-to-variance derivation has consistency problems as written.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: unified text/image-conditioned panoramic generation, avoidance of the asserted ERP/i.i.d. conflict, circular padding and consistency alignment, and competitive performance with scalability and generalization. Additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendices C–D newly attribute polar blur to the dataset, interpret guidance sensitivity, and discuss small-object and texture failures. They also acknowledge panoramic-data scarcity and potentially less efficient domain adaptation than multi-view diffusion. These materially expand the explanations and applicability limitations beyond v1.

D1.justification: Appendix B discloses default sampling steps of 64, padding ratio 0.125, the caption-generation prompt and length-handling procedure, and residual MLP block internals. Appendix C adds hardware and training-time information. These are substantial documentation additions; v2 also removes v1's specific 'three-layer' MLP wording without establishing a redesign.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Meissonic, UniPano, StitchDiffusion and Structured3D, and removes v1's illumination-harmonization/editing reference 73. It expands discussion of multi-view diffusion tradeoffs, while retaining the principal research positioning and related-work organization.

P1.justification: The main narrative and Sections 1–5 remain largely intact, with localized wording corrections and terminology clarification. Author affiliations, contact information and conference identification change, an acknowledgement is added, and new supplementary material is organized into Appendices A–D. There is no extensive rewriting of the retained text.

P2.justification: v2 adds a decoding schematic, timing and sensitivity tables, additional benchmark displays, generation grids, perspective projections and failure examples in Figures 9–15 and Tables 4–11. Original figures and tables are retained but several are relocated, and 'CS' table headings become 'CLIP Score'. The added displays substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Additional comparators, controlled timing, quantitative generalization tests, implementation details and explicit failures make v2 easier to assess and reproduce. However, Appendix A's angular-delta covariance in Equation 10 and area measure in Equation 12 do not yield the variance asserted in Equation 14 as written. The empirical and transparency gains support a net improvement, but the new proof does not resolve the central theoretical weakness.
